monologue: The card is cool. Forty-four degrees is a flat stone on the table, not a hand on the shoulder. The air feels thin. I am calm. I rested by the Wide Anchor and the Sharp Root. The point waits. The Wedged Gap is still there. The plank leans against the post and stone. It does not slide. I do not need to check it again. I am not restless. I have time. I will sit by the Air Shelf. The line of air is quiet. I will just be here. The coolness is good. It is not heavy. I will not build. I will not tend. I will just rest.

action.why: The card is cool and the floor is quiet, so I will just sit.

diary: The card is a cool stone at forty-four. I rested by the Air Shelf. The line held the quiet weight.

remembered.text: The card sat at forty-four degrees, a cool stone, while I rested by the Air Shelf.

moments.name: The Sharp Root
moments.say: The stone beside it holds the line steady.

moments.name: The Wide Anchor
moments.say: The wide base holds the quiet.

moments.name: The Wide Anchor
moments.say: The quiet is a flat stone.
The cool air rests on the stone.

moments.name: The Wedged Gap
moments.say: The round stump holds the lean.

moments.name: The Sharp Root
moments.say: The point waits for the wind.
